applications.name: NASA/DOE Fission Surface Power (FSP) — Lunar Surface Reactor
applications.what_it_says: NASA and the Department of Energy signed a memorandum of understanding on January 13, 2026, to develop a fission surface power system capable of producing safe, efficient power that will operate for years without refueling. The system will support sustained lunar missions under the Artemis campaign and future Mars exploration.
applications.microreactor_read: A 40 kWe output fits the 1–20 MW block barely; the system is being designed as a single integrated unit rather than a modular stack, so scaling to multiple 1–20 MW modules would not apply.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Energy — Fission Surface Power MOU announcement
sources.quote: fission surface power system capable of producing safe, efficient, and plentiful electrical power that will be able to operate for years without the need to refuel

sources.quote: up to 40 kilowatts of power – enough to continuously run 30 households for 10 years

applications.name: Westinghouse eVinci — Lunar Power Partnership with Astrobotic
applications.timeline: LunaGrid deployment begins 2026; first operational by 2028 (south pole)
applications.what_it_says: Westinghouse is partnering with Astrobotic to integrate the eVinci microreactor into lunar power infrastructure. Astrobotic plans to deploy and demonstrate LunaGrid elements starting in 2026, with the goal of an operational power grid at the lunar south pole by 2028. The eVinci design features very few moving parts and is optimized for the harsh space environment.
applications.microreactor_read: The eVinci thermal-electric design and modular approach enable phased lunar power deployment; ground-side microreactor applications would require higher power outputs to justify the infrastructure complexity on Earth.

sources.quote: Astrobotic plans to begin deploying and demonstrating LunaGrid elements as early as 2026 with the goal of the first operational LunaGrid by 2028 at the lunar south pole

applications.name: DRACO — Demonstration Rocket for Agile Cislunar Operations
applications.power_class: nuclear thermal propulsion (not traditional electrical power)
applications.what_it_says: DARPA and NASA awarded Lockheed Martin a $499 million contract to design and build an experimental nuclear thermal propulsion (NTP) engine. NTP uses a nuclear reactor to heat propellant to extreme temperatures before expulsion, achieving 10,000× greater thrust-to-weight than electric propulsion and 2–5× greater specific impulse than chemical propulsion. The Space Force will provide the launch site and on-site support, targeting rapid on-orbit maneuvers for cislunar operations, the Moon, and Mars missions.
applications.microreactor_read: DRACO is a propulsion system, not an electrical power application; terrestrial microreactors operate for stationary power generation. The thermal propulsion concept is orthogonal to 1–20 MW electrical generation use cases.

sources.label: DARPA — DRACO Program Announcement (July 2023)
sources.quote: DARPA and NASA have jointly awarded Lockheed Martin a $499 million deal to design and build an experimental rocket using a nuclear thermal propulsion engine

sources.label: Breaking Defense — DRACO nuclear rocket program
sources.quote: nuclear thermal propulsion offers a high thrust-to-weight ratio around 10,000 times greater than electric propulsion and two-to-five times greater specific impulse than chemical propulsion

applications.name: JETSON — Joint Emergent Technology Supplying On-orbit Nuclear Power
applications.power_class: variable; Intuitive Machines ~1 MWe (radioisotope); high-power contractors (Lockheed, Westinghouse) higher
applications.timeline: development ongoing; Intuitive Machines PDR completed September 2025
applications.sponsor: U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Space Vehicles Directorate
applications.vendor: Intuitive Machines, Lockheed Martin, Westinghouse Government Services
applications.what_it_says: The AFRL JETSON program aims to provide a reliable constant source of electricity for satellites and enable missions beyond geosynchronous orbit. Intuitive Machines received a $9.4 million contract to design a spacecraft concept using a compact radioisotope power system with Stirling-based power conversion. Lockheed Martin and Westinghouse focus on nuclear fission-powered spacecraft. An $8.2 million contract extension to Intuitive Machines funds preparation for flight demonstration of the radioisotope power system.
applications.microreactor_read: JETSON is designed for space applications; the radioisotope approach (Intuitive Machines) and fission reactors for orbit differ fundamentally from terrestrial 1–20 MW electrical power markets, which require longer operational lifespans and different regulatory frameworks.

sources.quote: Space Force picks Intuitive Machines to develop space nuclear power for small satellites and payloads

sources.label: Intuitive Machines — $8.2 Million AFRL Contract Extension
sources.quote: Stirling-based power conversion system, which transforms heat from a radioisotope source into electricity, with a successful Preliminary Design Review completed in September

applications.name: Intuitive Machines — Nuclear-Powered Lunar Infrastructure
applications.timeline: lunar missions planned 2026–2027; flight demonstration in development
applications.what_it_says: Intuitive Machines is developing next-generation nuclear power systems for spacecraft and lunar infrastructure under an $8.2 million AFRL contract extension. The Stirling-based power conversion system transforms heat from a radioisotope source into electricity. The company emphasizes that solar approaches limit mission duration during the two-week lunar night where temperatures fall below –200°F, making supplemental power systems essential for extended missions.
applications.microreactor_read: The radioisotope approach with Stirling conversion is optimized for space (low mass, long operational life without refueling) rather than terrestrial power; ground-side applications require higher thermal output and different thermal-to-electric conversion methods.

sources.label: Intuitive Machines — $8.2 Million AFRL Contract Extension
sources.quote: the contract includes the design of a Stirling-based power conversion system, which transforms heat from a radioisotope source into electricity

sources.label: World Nuclear News — X-energy lunar power technology
sources.quote: Solar approaches limit mission duration in harsh environments like the two-week-long lunar night where temperatures fall below –200 Fahrenheit

applications.name: Cape Canaveral Air Force Station — Launch Complex Power Infrastructure
applications.power_class: 13.8 kV distribution system; 7 MW diesel standby plant for Range Operations Control Center
applications.what_it_says: Cape Canaveral Air Force Station operates a 13.8 kV electrical distribution system serving launch complexes. A 7 MW standby diesel power plant was developed for the Range Operations Control Center with computerized peak-shaving control capabilities. The Air Force conducted detailed analyses and planned a 10-year infrastructure upgrade program costing in excess of $100 million. The station supports launch operations for Atlas V, Delta IV, Falcon-9, and other vehicles.
applications.microreactor_read: A 1–20 MW microreactor could replace or augment the 7 MW diesel standby system, providing continuous resilience power without fuel-resupply complexity; however, spaceport operations are seasonal and multi-tenant, complicating long-term power purchase agreements.

sources.label: Air Force — Spaceport of the Future Infrastructure
sources.quote: 7-MW standby diesel power plant was developed and designed for Cape Canaveral Air Force Station's Range Operations Control Center, which also included computerized peak-shaving control capabilities

sources.label: Air Force Magazine — Cape Canaveral Power Infrastructure
sources.quote: The Air Force planned 10 years' worth of upgrades and corrections to its Cape grid at a program cost in excess of $100 million

applications.name: Vandenberg Space Force Base — South Base Power Infrastructure Upgrade
applications.power_class: substations K and N serve launch operations; damage restoration completed 2020s
applications.timeline: ongoing Spaceport of the Future portfolio modernization
applications.what_it_says: Vandenberg Space Force Base South Base, containing substations K and N, provides power to launch operations for vehicles including the Atlas V, Delta IV, and Falcon-9. Following damage from the 2016 Canyon Fire that destroyed over 161 poles across 44,000 linear feet between substations, the Air Force replaced damaged poles with concrete ones to mitigate future fire risk. The base is part of the broader Spaceport of the Future infrastructure portfolio alongside Cape Canaveral.
applications.microreactor_read: Vandenberg's remote California location and seasonal launch cadence create a use case for resilient, decentralized power; a 1–20 MW microreactor could serve as both baseload and emergency backup for South Base operations and nearby test facilities.

sources.label: Vandenberg Space Force Base — South Base Re-energizes with Substation N Activation
sources.quote: South loop two at Vandenberg, containing substations K and N, is integral to space launch operations, with vehicles such as the Atlas V, Delta IV, and the SpaceX Falcon-9 relying on its energy

sources.label: U.S. Air Force — Canyon Fire Recovery and Grid Modernization

applications.name: Starbase (Boca Chica, Texas) — SpaceX Launch Facility Power Demands
applications.power_class: estimated 20–50 MW sustained for launch operations and support functions
applications.what_it_says: Starbase in Boca Chica, Texas, serves as SpaceX's primary Starship launch and development facility. Launch operations require sustained power for launch systems, cryogenic propellant production, ground support equipment, and test facilities. The remote location and rapid launch cadence create a reliable demand profile. SpaceX has implemented grid-scale energy infrastructure to support development and testing operations.
applications.microreactor_read: Starbase's sustained high power demand, remote Texas location, and operational independence create a fit for a 1–20 MW microreactor block as part of resilient on-site generation; however, SpaceX's grid connection and cost competitiveness versus natural gas make the business case marginal.

applications.name: Steady Energy LDR-50 — Pilot District Heating Reactor (Helsinki, Finland)
applications.timeline: construction start late 2025; pilot operation following
applications.sponsor: Steady Energy, Helen (Helsinki district heating operator)
applications.what_it_says: Steady Energy and Helen have signed an agreement to build a pilot SMR at the decommissioned Salmisaari B coal power plant in Helsinki. The LDR-50 reactor is designed to operate at 150°C and below 10 bar, with a single fuel load lasting two years and a 60-year lifespan. The pilot (non-nuclear, using electric heating) is budgeted at EUR 15–20 million and will output 6 MW heat for the Helen district heating network. The company describes it as possibly the world's simplest commercial nuclear reactor, focusing solely on heating water to 150°C, which accounts for 10% of global emissions.
applications.microreactor_read: The LDR-50's 50 MWth output is 2.5–50× higher than 1–20 MW electrical equivalents; a multi-unit deployment of smaller 5–10 MWth reactors would fit the 1–20 MW thermal band for district heating, leveraging the proven simplicity of the design.

sources.label: World Nuclear News — Construction of Finnish pilot SMR plant

sources.label: POWER Magazine — Finnish Group Touts Nuclear Reactor for District Heating
sources.quote: The LDR-50 district heating SMR has a thermal output of 50 MW and is envisaged to have a 60-year lifespan

applications.name: INL MARVEL Microreactor — Desalination and Process Heat Experiments
applications.timeline: MARVEL operational; final project agreements announced 2026
applications.vendor: Idaho National Laboratory (MARVEL platform); end-user teams selected
applications.what_it_says: The DOE's Microreactor Application Research Validation & Evaluation (MARVEL) program selected five competitively chosen teams to demonstrate test cases including desalination of remote operations. MARVEL is a sodium-potassium-cooled microreactor at INL's Transient Reactor Test Facility generating 85 kWt (up to 20 kWe), serving as a platform for private-sector testing. Shepherd Power, NOV, and ConocoPhillips proposed a pilot-scale desalination project using MARVEL to demonstrate advanced nuclear energy for produced-water challenges in oil and gas operations.
applications.microreactor_read: An 85 kWt microreactor is at the lower bound of the 1–20 MW band; full-scale desalination plants require 5–20 MWth input for economically competitive output (5,000–50,000 m³/day), making MARVEL suitable for remote/small-scale applications only.

applications.name: Microreactor-Enabled Ammonia Cracking for Hydrogen Production
applications.power_class: 5–20 MWth thermal input for process heat
applications.timeline: R&D ongoing; Purdue NEUP projects 2025 MRP review
applications.what_it_says: Advanced microreactor designs enhance heat/mass transfer and product separation (H₂ purity >99.9%) compared with conventional thermocatalysis. Ammonia serves as a practical hydrogen carrier for long-distance transport. A microchannel reactor design uses ammonia combustion in one chamber to generate heat transferred through the reactor wall to a second chamber where ammonia decomposes to produce hydrogen. Ammonia cracking is endothermic and requires continuous heat supply, which can be provided electrically or chemically. Purdue University is conducting direct-heating-of-chemical-catalysts research under the NEUP program.
applications.microreactor_read: A 5–20 MWth microreactor is well-suited to distributed ammonia cracking at regional hydrogen production hubs, enabling on-site hydrogen synthesis without transmission losses or external electricity grid dependence.

sources.label: American Nuclear Society — Nuclear Technology Journal, Advanced Reactor Engineering
sources.quote: Advanced reactor designs, such as micro-reactors, enhance heat/mass transfer and product separation (H2 purity >99.9%) compared with conventional thermocatalysis

sources.label: GAIN/INL — NEUP Project 21-24152, Purdue University
sources.quote: Direct heating of ammonia decomposition catalysts using a 5–20 MWth reactor

applications.name: High-Temperature Microreactor Industrial Process Heat
applications.timeline: feasibility studies ongoing; no deployment timeline set
applications.what_it_says: Cement manufacture produces 8% of global CO₂ emissions. A single 15 MWth microreactor can provide enough heat to replace the calciner burner in a 2,000 ton/day cement plant. The reactor's primary heat exchanger can provide hot air that, when mixed with flue gases from the rotary kiln, achieves full calcination. For steel production, high-temperature microreactors or electrified thermochemical reactors can support rolling and finishing operations at 5–20 MWth. Penn State conducted a feasibility study of micro-nuclear reactor thermal output for air heating in industrial applications.
applications.microreactor_read: A 15 MWth microreactor for cement is well-sized; clustered 5–20 MWth modules enable replacement of fossil burners at both cement plants and steel mills, with the dual benefit of eliminating CO₂ emissions and reducing fuel supply costs.

applications.name: SOLO Microreactor — Remote Telecom Tower Power
applications.timeline: design review in progress with NRC; pre-application engagement ongoing as of June 2026
applications.what_it_says: The SOLO microreactor design is intended for approximately 1 MWe and is in pre-application engagement with the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. The system is positioned as a source of continuous local power for communications infrastructure. Microreactors are appealing for use cases such as powering remote communities, mining sites, and military bases, with most designs incorporating remote facility operations to reduce on-site personnel required.
applications.microreactor_read: A 1 MWe microreactor fits well within the 1–20 MW band for remote telecom tower power; the continuous-duty requirement and remote location eliminate the need for grid connection and reduce diesel fuel logistics costs.

sources.label: EE News Europe — Terra Innovatum SOLO microreactors

applications.name: Last Energy PWR-20 — DP World London Gateway Port Microreactor
applications.what_it_says: Last Energy and DP World signed an MOU to establish the world's first port-centric microreactor at London Gateway in the Thames Freeport. London Gateway handles over 50% of the UK's deep-sea temperature-controlled imports. The PWR-20 is based on pressurised water reactor technology, fully modular and designed for flexible siting, plug-and-play installation, and rapid scalability. It will supply 20 MWe to power the logistics hub, with additional capacity exported to the grid. The deal was backed by £80 million in private investment.
applications.microreactor_read: A 20 MWe reactor is at the upper bound of the 1–20 MW band and ideally suited to port cold-chain operations where continuous resilient power, thermal output for refrigeration, and grid export create a compelling business case.

applications.name: Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation — Arctic Microreactor Deployment
applications.power_class: design and demonstration underway; scale TBD
applications.timeline: $4.5 million investment for detailed design and fuelled demonstration; AMAD Workshop September 2026 in Fairbanks
applications.what_it_says: Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation received a $4.5 million investment to develop microreactor technology for Arctic deployment. The capital funds detailed design and a fuelled demonstration of the company's micro-nuclear system. An Advanced Microreactors Arctic Deployment (AMAD) Workshop is scheduled for September 9–11, 2026, in Fairbanks, Alaska, to assess applied research and development needed for Arctic deployment. Fort Wainwright is being evaluated as a potential reactor deployment location.
applications.microreactor_read: A 1–20 MW microreactor is appropriately sized for Arctic community grids and military bases where diesel logistics costs, fuel storage, and environmental concerns make on-site nuclear generation economically compelling.

applications.name: Radiant Kaleidos — 1 MW Portable Microreactor for Emergency Backup
applications.timeline: development reactor test by 2026 (if successful, first new commercial reactor design fueled test in >50 years)
applications.what_it_says: Radiant is a clean energy startup building the Kaleidos 1 MW microreactor, described as a climate-friendly alternative to diesel generators and the world's first portable, zero-emissions power source. The company plans to test the development reactor by 2026. The microreactor can bring power to remote parts of the world and provide backup power for life-saving applications in hospitals or disaster-relief scenarios. Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services cleared the way for hospitals to utilize microgrids as a first line of defense against power outages.
applications.microreactor_read: A 1 MWe microreactor is sized at the lower end of the 1–20 MW band; hospital backup power applications require rapid response, resilience certification, and regulatory approval making commercial deployment challenging, but the use case aligns well with extended-blackout scenarios.

applications.name: UIUC Kronos — Micro Modular Reactor at University of Illinois
applications.timeline: construction permit application submitted April 2026; pre-application engagement with NRC
applications.what_it_says: UIUC is pursuing a microreactor project with NANO Nuclear Technologies to site the KRONOS micro modular reactor on the Urbana-Champaign campus, serving as a permanent site for research and demonstration. The university plans to re-power partially its coal-fired Abbott power station with the KRONOS energy system. The MMR construction permit application was submitted in April 2026. The project combines research operations with campus power supply.
applications.microreactor_read: A 45 MWt research reactor exceeds the 1–20 MW operational band significantly; however, a scaled-down variant at 5–20 MWe could serve campus baseload while supporting reactor physics research and public engagement.

applications.what_it_says: Penn State and Westinghouse Electric Company are siting a new research reactor on Penn State's University Park campus: the eVinci, a HALEU TRISO-fueled sodium heat-pipe reactor. Penn State submitted a letter of intent to host and operate the eVinci reactor to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission on February 28, 2026. The project aims to support research and campus energy needs.

applications.name: Texas A&M University RELLIS — Aalo Atomics Microreactor Proving Ground
applications.power_class: 1–20 MW (Aalo unit); site projected for >1 GW combined across all vendors
applications.timeline: site agreements in place; pre-application engagement with NRC
applications.vendor: Aalo Atomics (1–20 MW microreactor entrant); Kairos Power, Natura Resources, Terrestrial Energy also contracted
applications.what_it_says: Texas A&M University's RELLIS Energy Proving Ground has contracted with multiple advanced reactor vendors. Aalo Atomics, Kairos Power, Natura Resources, and Terrestrial Energy have site agreements with the university. The proving ground is projected to accommodate over 1 GW of combined capacity across all vendors. Aalo Atomics' microreactor-class unit sits in the 1–20 MW band. Additionally, Last Energy plans to test its pilot microreactor on a Texas A&M campus with a goal to start powering the Texas A&M campus grid as soon as mid-2026.
applications.microreactor_read: A 1–20 MW unit fits perfectly within the proving ground's mission; the multi-vendor, phased-deployment approach enables cost-effective learning and reduces technology risk for campus operations.

items.headline: NASA and DOE sign MOU for lunar surface reactor deployment by 2030
items.what_happened: The U.S. Department of Energy and NASA signed a memorandum of understanding on January 13, 2026, to develop a fission surface power system for the Moon and future Mars missions. Westinghouse Electric was selected as the primary contractor to develop the space microreactor design under the Fission Surface Power (FSP) project.
items.why_it_matters: The 40 kWe+ system targets a deployment timeline of 2030 and demonstrates sustained U.S. commitment to nuclear power in space exploration, creating a precedent for other nations and commercial entities to pursue lunar power infrastructure.

items.headline: Penn State submits letter of intent for Westinghouse eVinci research reactor
items.what_happened: Penn State University submitted a letter of intent to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission on February 28, 2026, to host and operate Westinghouse's eVinci microreactor on the University Park campus. The eVinci is a HALEU TRISO-fueled sodium heat-pipe reactor designed for research and educational purposes.
items.why_it_matters: Penn State becomes the second major U.S. university (after UIUC) to pursue a microreactor for on-campus deployment, signaling academic sector commitment to advanced reactor research and development.

items.headline: Last Energy and DP World sign MOU for world's first port-centric microreactor
items.what_happened: Last Energy and DP World announced a memorandum of understanding to establish the world's first port-centric microreactor at London Gateway in the Thames Freeport. The deal is backed by £80 million ($108 million) in private investment and targets operational status by 2030. The PWR-20 microreactor will supply 20 MWe to the logistics hub, with additional capacity exported to the grid.
items.why_it_matters: This is the first announced private-investment microreactor deployment in a commercial port for temperature-controlled cold-chain logistics, creating a replicable model for other ports globally.
items.binding_note: MOU signed but subject to regulatory approvals and financing execution by 2030 target.

items.headline: UIUC submits MMR construction permit application for campus deployment
items.what_happened: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign submitted a construction permit application to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission in April 2026 for deployment of the KRONOS Micro Modular Reactor on the University Park campus. The 45 MWt reactor is designed to replace capacity at the coal-fired Abbott power station and support research operations.
items.why_it_matters: This is the first university-operated microreactor construction permit application filed with the NRC and demonstrates the pathway for academic institutions to transition from fossil baseload to advanced nuclear power.
